synth.title: Tap-target + slip-adjacency sweep
synth.principle_summary: Two distinct, non-overlapping mechanics govern interactive-target safety, and a computable sweep has to check both separately, not conflate them. (1) Raw target-size geometry is Fitts's-Law-grounded and has a settled, standards-authored floor: WCAG 2.5.8 (AA, WCAG 2.2, not 2.1) sets 24x24 CSS px or a 24px center-to-center spacing exception (five named exceptions apply); WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA) sets a stricter 44x44 with no spacing escape hatch; Apple HIG independently lands at 44x44pt (60x60pt visionOS); Material lands at 48dp with an 8dp recommended gap. Solen's own 44px design-contract floor sits deliberately at the AAA/HIG line, above the legal AA minimum, not a restatement of it, so SOURCE.md:1032 citing "WCAG 2.1" for that 44px number is a real, fixable citation error. (2) Slip adjacency is a separate mechanic no mainstream tool checks: when a destructive control (cancel, delete) sits near a benign or commit control, the risk is not "is this tappable" but "can this be tapped BY MISTAKE instead of its neighbor," a function of inter-target distance AND consequence asymmetry. The real-world scouting confirms slip adjacency is solved industry-wide not by spacing alone but by at least one of three differentiation channels: a distinct hue for the destructive action, a downgraded control type/weight (text link vs filled button), or spatial/structural separation (a second screen, an overflow menu, or a mandatory confirmation step) — same-size, same-color, side-by-side pairs (Shift's reschedule/cancel row) are the industry's own worst-practice example, not a defensible baseline.

real_world_evidence.what: Reschedule and Cancel are two stacked full-width list rows (~52-56px each, hairline divider), both neutral black, no color differentiation; low slip-risk because both are equally low-consequence entry points and the actual destructive commit is deferred to a second confirmation screen reached one more tap away.

Sole black "Yes, cancel" button at the bottom; no adjacent Back/No button exists at all, the only escape is the top-left chevron, physically far from the commit target. Also matches Fresha's staff-side pattern (Fresha Help Center) where cancellation is gated behind a status dropdown or overflow menu, never a bare button beside Reschedule/Edit.

Reschedule (solid primary) stacked above Cancel instead, rendered as a plain TEXT LINK not a button, i.e. control-type downgrade removes adjacency risk entirely since the two aren't even the same control class.
Reschedule (solid blue fill) stacked above Cancel (outline, same blue text) with a visible ~12-16px vertical gap; differentiated by fill weight (solid vs outline) plus a real gap, not touching edges.

Reschedule and Cancel sit side by side, same-width, same neutral outline style, ~12-16px gap, zero color or weight differentiation, only the label text differs. Flagged in the scouting report as the weakest pattern found, the anti-pattern this sweep exists to catch.

Two side-by-side 50/50-split full-width buttons, No (light gray) and Yes, cancel (green), adjacent with only a thin gap, differentiated purely by hue. Shows that even a top-tier app accepts side-by-side adjacency for a binary confirm/cancel when color does the differentiation work.

Destructive Delete sits directly adjacent to benign Mute/Archive with ZERO visual gap, only a hard color boundary; mitigated by (a) requiring a deliberate swipe gesture rather than a single tap and (b) consistently placing the destructive segment last/hardest to reach.
Single-action swipe reveal (Delete only, no sibling action in the same gesture), so no within-gesture adjacency risk exists; the only separation is full row height to the next list item.
Swipe-up, then tap Cancel, then a second explicit confirm tap ("Yes, Cancel"): friction-added two-step plus a directional gesture, not a single adjacent button.

real_world_evidence.source: Airbnb, cancel-a-reservation flow (Airbnb Help, guest + host)
real_world_evidence.what: Cancel reservation sits physically separated (top-right) from the page's other primary actions, then requires reason-select then Continue then a second Cancel-reservation tap with a refund breakdown shown before final commit.

Cancel button sits at the bottom of the reservation-details page, separated from Modify, gated by a reason-select and fee-disclosure screen before the cancellation is final. Styling reported as inconsistent across surfaces by third parties, so treat only the placement/gating claim as reliable, not the color claim.

Confirmation names the consequence (e.g. cancellation-deadline penalty) before a second confirm tap. Complaints center on appointment-list findability, a DIFFERENT failure mode (can't find the right item) than slip-adjacency (hit the wrong control); worth keeping the two failure categories distinct in the sweep's scope.

real_world_evidence.source: NN/g, "Dangerous UX: Consequential Options Close to Benign Options" (cited across 2025 practitioner sources)
real_world_evidence.what: Named, canonical practitioner doctrine ranking destructive-neutral proximity as a top-10 application design mistake; convention is neutral/Cancel first, destructive second, with a confirmation modal as the standard extra-friction pattern.

Cites WCAG 2.5.8's own spacing-exception language verbatim: a target is compliant if, when a 24px-diameter circle is centered on its bounding box, the circle does not intersect another target's circle. This is the closest thing to a computable slip-adjacency rule that already has spec authority, worth citing directly instead of inventing a new heuristic.

real_world_evidence.source: Social/trend scout, Muzli 2026 mobile UI trends + LogRocket swipe accessibility piece
real_world_evidence.what: No social/trend content addresses tap-target sizing or slip-adjacency directly (the topic lives in accessibility/practitioner blogs, not TikTok/Instagram design content). The one live directional pull found is gesture-first compound gestures with haptic layering (swipe-to-delete replacing tap flows), which LogRocket explicitly warns needs a tap-based fallback or it excludes users with motor impairments. No unsourced viral stat was found on this topic either, an honest gap, not a myth to screen out.

synth.generative_prior: CHECK A (target-size floor, extends the already-speced axe-core wire-in): BLOCKING tier = WCAG 2.5.8 AA, min(w,h) < 24px CSS AND no same-type neighbor center >= 24px away (the exact spec test: a 24px-diameter circle centered on each element's bounding box must not intersect another target's circle, per DubBot/W3C). ADVISORY tier = Solen's own 44px design-contract floor (RATIONALE.md:157, the AAA/HIG line), flagged separately since axe-core has no concept of it. Real-app calibration: none of the 8 apps scouted render a full-width action row under 48-56px tall (Fresha's list rows, CVS's buttons), which is comfortably above both floors, confirming 44px is the de facto industry target even where 24px is the legal minimum. CHECK B (slip adjacency, net-new): for any pair of tagged elements where one is "destructive" and the other is "commit" or "neutral", FLAG if edgeGap < 24px UNLESS at least ONE of three real-app-confirmed differentiation channels is present: (a) HUE differentiation, the destructive control uses a distinct color from the commit control (Lime's green/gray split, the near-universal pattern across all 8 apps scouted except Shift), (b) CONTROL-TYPE/WEIGHT downgrade, destructive rendered as a lower-weight control class than commit, e.g. text link vs filled button (Redfin), outline vs solid fill (CVS), or buried behind a menu/dropdown (Fresha staff-side), or (c) STRUCTURAL separation, destructive reached via a different screen, gated by a mandatory intermediate step (reason-select, second confirm tap: Uber, Airbnb, Booking.com, Fresha, Doctolib all use this, a 5/5 convergence), or physically isolated from the primary action zone (Fresha's confirm-screen chevron pattern). Shift's row (same size, same hue, same weight, same screen, 12-16px gap only) is the sweep's canonical FAIL example: it has none of the three channels. BOUNDARY / tension to flag, not resolve here: every real app scouted uses a distinct HUE for destructive actions (red, orange, or at minimum green-vs-gray for confirm/cancel); Solen's locked ink-only CTA system (`bg-s-ink` for the one commit button) has no destructive-action color token defined anywhere in LOCKFILE/SOURCE. This sweep cannot assume channel (a) is available to Solen without a separate, explicitly-owner-approved decision to add a destructive hue (likely the existing error-red token); until that decision is made, Solen destructive actions must rely on channel (b) or (c) instead, and the sweep's channel-detection logic needs a Solen-specific default of "no hue channel available" rather than assuming red-vs-ink reads as differentiated.
synth.proposed_addition:
COMPUTABLE METRIC SPEC (RATIONALE.md §28 lens B, D6, extends the S15 baseline draft with real-app calibration):

CHECK A: Solen-floor target-size sweep. rect = element.getBoundingClientRect() (outer hit element, not painted glyph, e.g. HeartButton's 44 outer/32 inner). BLOCKING: min(w,h) < 24px AND not exempt (WCAG 2.5.8 AA; reuse axe-core's target-size rule verbatim, axe-core 4.5+, and set the WCAG 2.2 ruleset flag explicitly, since the rule ships OFF by default and silently no-ops otherwise, a wiring detail confirmed against Deque's own release notes). ADVISORY: min(w,h) < 44px AND not exempt AND not on the named Solen exception list (TabPill 32/40px, SaveHeart 28x28, already documented SACRIFICES). Exempt = inline text targets or the named exception list.

CHECK B: Slip-adjacency sweep (net-new). Tag interactive elements with a CONSEQUENCE attribute (data-consequence="commit"|"destructive"|"neutral") per component type, not per instance. For every pair where consequence differs and at least one side is commit or destructive: edgeGap = shortest gap between bounding boxes. FLAG if edgeGap < 24px UNLESS one of three differentiation channels is present, each drawn from a converged real-app pattern rather than invented: (a) hue channel, distinct color between the two controls, (b) control-type/weight channel, different control class or fill weight (button vs link, solid vs outline, or buried behind a menu), (c) structural channel, destructive gated behind a second screen or mandatory confirm step. Output per flagged pair: both selectors, both tags, edgeGap, which channel (if any) was detected. Size-ratio asymmetry (the original 1.5x-area guess) folds into channel (b) rather than standing alone, since none of the 8 scouted apps use pure size difference without also changing hue or weight.

BOUNDARY (flag, do not resolve): Solen's ink-only CTA system currently has no destructive-hue token; every real app scouted differentiates destructive actions by color. This sweep's channel-(a) detection defaults to "unavailable" for Solen until an explicit owner decision adds a destructive hue (candidate: the existing error-red token), so today's implementations must lean on channels (b)/(c).

CITATION FIX (same gap-register item, still standing from the baseline draft, verified unchanged): replace SOURCE.md:1032's "Minimum 44x44 px hit area per WCAG 2.1 (some platforms 48)" with RATIONALE.md:157's already-correct framing (24x24 WCAG 2.5.8 AA legal floor; 44px is Solen's voluntary AAA/HIG-line choice, WCAG 2.2 not 2.1).

DISTINCT-FAILURE-MODE NOTE (from Doctolib scouting, worth a line in the sweep's scope doc): "can't find the right control among many" (Doctolib's actual user complaint) is a findability problem, not slip-adjacency; the sweep should not conflate the two when triaging flagged pairs.

TASTE LAB PROBE: unchanged core design, now anchored to real frames instead of abstract renders: show the Lime pair (hue-only, no gap), the Shift pair (no channel, small gap), and the CVS pair (weight + gap) side by side at the same size, ask which feels "safe to tap without double-checking." Use the answer to convert the currently-guessed channel-sufficiency question (is hue-alone, per Lime, actually enough, or does it need to pair with a gap too) into a locked rule, since Lime is real-world evidence that top apps DO ship hue-only differentiation at close proximity, which the draft's original probe didn't have a real anchor for.

synth.taste_lab_probe: Anchor the probe to real frames instead of abstract renders: show the Lime confirm pair (hue-only differentiation, gray vs green, thin gap), the Shift reschedule/cancel pair (no differentiation channel, ~12-16px gap, industry's own worst example), and the CVS Health pair (weight differentiation, solid vs outline, ~12-16px gap), all resized to the same on-screen dimensions, and ask "which pair feels safe to tap without double-checking." Use the answer to settle whether a single differentiation channel (hue alone, per Lime) is sufficient on its own or must pair with a minimum gap, replacing the original draft's unanchored 1.5x size-ratio guess with a decision grounded in what top apps already ship.

myths_caught: NN/g "Dangerous UX: Consequential Options Close to Benign Options" is cited in sources[] as a named canonical NN/g article/doctrine (T2). I could not find this article on nngroup.com's own article index, and targeted web/search checks (Bing, DuckDuckGo, Google) returned no corroboration of this exact title as an NN/g-authored piece. This is the same failure pattern the myth_screen guards against: a specific claim dressed in a prestigious org's name without a traceable citation. Downgraded to CONV (a real, well-observed practitioner convention, independently supported by the 8-app Mobbin convergence in this same draft) rather than verified NN/g doctrine. Do not cite this as "NN/g names X as a top-10 mistake" in the shipped RATIONALE entry without a working URL.

Apple HIG's "60x60pt on visionOS" figure could not be verified this session: Apple's HIG pages are JS-rendered and returned only page titles to WebFetch, and no secondary source corroborated the specific visionOS number (the general 44x44pt iOS/iPadOS figure is well-corroborated and kept at T1, but the visionOS addendum is unverified, not confirmed-false, and should not be treated as settled until directly checked).
verified.residual_risks:
Two items need a follow-up check before being treated as locked, and one item is a genuine owner-decision fork already correctly deferred by the draft:
(1) Apple HIG "60x60pt visionOS" figure is unverified this pass (JS-rendered docs blocked automated fetch) — spot-check directly against developer.apple.com before citing it as settled fact; the core 44x44pt figure is fine.
(2) The NN/g "Dangerous UX" article title could not be located — either find the real URL or rewrite the RATIONALE citation to describe it as converged practitioner convention (backed by the Mobbin 8-app evidence) rather than a named NN/g piece.
(3) OWNER-DECISION (carried from the draft's own BOUNDARY section, not resolved here): Solen's locked ink-only CTA system has no destructive-hue token, so slip-adjacency channel (a) — hue differentiation — is unavailable to Solen today. This is a genuine QUESTIONS.md candidate: does Solen want a destructive-red token (candidate: existing error-red), or does it commit to always using channel (b)/(c) (control-type downgrade or structural gating) for destructive actions? Do not silently add a red CTA token to resolve this.
(4) The proposed data-consequence="commit"|"destructive"|"neutral" tagging convention is net-new with no existing Solen precedent; sweeping every destructive/commit control to add it is real, unscoped implementation work, not a documentation-only change.
(5) Mobbin app-pattern evidence (Fresha, Redfin, CVS, Shift, Lime, Telegram/Shopee, MyFitnessPal, Uber, Airbnb, Doctolib) could not be independently re-audited this verify pass (no Mobbin access this session); the draft's own tiering is already conservative and self-correcting (Booking.com/Houst correctly downgraded to T3 for the styling claim), so no change made, but a live spot-check is worth doing before this becomes reference material other streams build on.
(6) EU Accessibility Act's link to WCAG 2.5.8 runs through EN 301 549, not a direct EAA-to-WCAG citation; the June 28 2025 enforcement date itself is confirmed (Level Access, secondary source) but "makes 2.5.8 a legal compliance floor" compresses a two-step legal chain — fine as a directional claim in a design rationale doc, not precise enough to cite in a legal-compliance context.
